signals.title: Scam losses keep denting digital-payment trust
signals.summary: Online scam losses reached 9.3 billion baht over seven months, and the damage is now being framed as a drag on confidence in the digital economy itself. The issue has moved from a consumer-protection story to an economic one.
signals.soWhat: Trust — not features — is becoming the binding constraint on digital payment growth, so fraud-prevention UX deserves roadmap space normally reserved for new products.

signals.title: Thai shoppers screen purchases through AI before buying
signals.summary: Research points to around 90% of Thai consumers using AI tools to vet products before purchase, while marketplace data highlights "ask-AI-first" behaviour alongside emotional and reassurance-driven shopping. Discovery is shifting away from traditional search and ads.
signals.soWhat: If AI assistants now sit between the brand and the buyer, product data quality and machine-readability start to matter more than ad spend.

signals.title: SME AI adoption is blocked by legacy IT, not by willingness
signals.summary: Thai SMEs are accelerating AI adoption but repeatedly stall on internal IT constraints. Commentary is calling for local content and programmes that pull SMEs into the new value chain.
signals.soWhat: The winning SME product is integration-light — something that works on top of messy existing systems rather than demanding a platform migration.

signals.title: Global AI and capital flow into the Thai startup ecosystem
signals.summary: International AI players are actively courting Thailand’s next wave of startups, while a Thai-founded venture raised roughly USD 270 million to become one of Southeast Asia’s most valuable startups. Outside capital and platform attention are arriving together.
signals.soWhat: Talent and distribution partnerships will get more competitive quickly — early positioning with these platforms is cheaper now than in twelve months.

signals.title: Data-centre buildout runs into water and power limits
signals.summary: Thailand’s data-centre ambitions are being weighed against the strategic question of how to participate in the AI infrastructure wave. Reporting is surfacing the real resource cost in water and electricity.
signals.soWhat: Compute-heavy roadmaps carry an energy and sustainability exposure that will become a procurement and reputational issue, not just a cost line.

signals.title: Policy pivots growth toward new industrial engines
signals.summary: Planners are pushing to escape a low-growth trap by accelerating four new engines — modern agriculture, upstream chips, pharma and medical devices, and future food. The central bank is simultaneously urging faster investment.
signals.soWhat: Public funding and incentives will concentrate in these four verticals, which is where partnership and pilot budgets are most likely to appear.

signals.title: Capital-market vehicles mobilise behind the new economy
signals.summary: A 1-billion-baht PE trust is being set up to back startups and new-economy businesses, alongside further programmes to deepen the capital market. A major local WealthTech platform has filed for IPO.
signals.soWhat: A domestic exit path is opening up, which changes the calculus for founders who previously assumed offshore listing was the only route.

signals.title: Customer experience is slipping while AI fails to reassure
signals.summary: Research indicates Thai customer-experience quality has declined and that AI is not yet generating full customer confidence. In parallel, commentary stresses how quickly consumers now switch away.
signals.soWhat: Deploying AI into service journeys without a visible trust mechanism risks accelerating churn rather than reducing cost.

signals.title: Growth forecast nudged up on investment momentum
signals.summary: A major bank research house raised its Thai GDP forecast for the year on the back of investment momentum and government measures. The revision is modest but directionally positive.
signals.soWhat: A slightly better macro backdrop supports budget conversations that were previously deferred, particularly investment-led ones.

signals.title: Chinese media consumption reshapes Thai consumer influence
signals.summary: New research highlights how audiences consuming Chinese media platforms are changing influence patterns among Thai consumers. Channel mix for reaching some segments is shifting.
signals.soWhat: Influence is fragmenting beyond the usual local platforms, so audience measurement built only on domestic channels will understate real reach.
